key_insight: A governed AI agent can coordinate an end-to-end biomedical research workflow while keeping protected data inside institutional boundaries and still produce expert-level GWAS results.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals and research teams run faster, more reproducible discovery studies on real-world patient data without broad data exposure.
method: Reviewed and planned the study workflow before execution
Orchestrated governed cohort extraction, GWAS analysis, QC, and evidence tracking
Used scientist-in-the-loop review to refine the hypertension phenotype and validate outputs
evidence_signal: In a hypertension GWAS on hospital-linked genotype and EHR data from 286,422 individuals, the system reproduced known loci such as FGF5, ATP2B1, CNNM2, FTO, and GRB14, with FGF5 reaching about -log10(p) ~ 70.
watch_item: Results depend on careful human oversight and phenotype definition, and the system’s value may be limited by institutional governance, data quality, and workflow integration.
paper_title: NVAITC AI Scientist: A Governed End-to-End Research System -- A Hypertension GWAS Case Study
